title: Mutual NDA playbook, recipient-weighted (Ashgrove Logistics, Party 2)
provenance: Draft, 15 October 2026 (BENCHMARK-V2.md P1), for layer A v2: the recipient-weighted position set over the 17 rule ids of the ContractNLI NDA playbook (contractnli/playbook-nda.json, whose balanced positions are unchanged). Our standard terms are the Common Paper Mutual NDA Version 1.0 with the cover terms of v2/base-nda.json, so the clean copy meets every preferred position; the two NDA position sets differ in which direction of change is a departure and how far each side will go. Each rule's source records the Common Paper text or annotation it rests on. Written by us with Claude Opus 5.5 (disclosed); fictional parties; not legal advice; not lawyer validated; not frozen until the ambiguity read (P2) and calibration (P8).

rules.title: How confidential information is identified
rules.guidance: We receive designs and pricing and need to know what we must protect. The two-limb test of the Standard Terms is our standard; a stricter marking regime helps us.
rules.preferred: Information is Confidential Information if the Disclosing Party identifies it as confidential or proprietary, or if it should reasonably be understood as confidential from its nature and the circumstances of disclosure.
rules.acceptable: Marking or written identification required for documents, with oral disclosures protected only if identified as confidential at the time.
rules.escalation: All information disclosed treated as confidential regardless of identification or reasonable understanding, or the definition extended to information disclosed before the Effective Date.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1 (two limbs: identified as confidential, or reasonably understood as confidential). Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): "some companies require marking", with a suggested edit removing the "reasonably understood" prong; the page also notes the definition does not reach information disclosed before the Effective Date and offers an edit extending it.

rules.title: Scope of confidential information
rules.guidance: We must be able to tell what is protected. The definition covers what the Disclosing Party discloses or makes available, nothing beyond.
rules.preferred: A definition limited to information disclosed or made available by the Disclosing Party, with the Standard Terms' list of examples.
rules.escalation: The definition extended beyond what the Disclosing Party discloses or makes available: for example to information about the Disclosing Party obtained from other sources, to analyses, notes or other material we create from it, or to information of the Disclosing Party's affiliates or customers.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1 list (technical or business information, product designs or roadmaps, requirements, pricing, security and compliance documentation, technology, inventions and know-how). The page gives "vendor security documentation" as an example of what an NDA protects.

rules.title: Oral and visual disclosures
rules.guidance: Oral and visual disclosures are protected under the same reasonable-understanding test as documents; we cannot accept a regime where everything seen on a visit is confidential.
rules.preferred: Information is protected in whatever form it is disclosed or made available, under the same identification or reasonable-understanding test.
rules.acceptable: Oral and visual disclosures protected only if identified as confidential when made or confirmed in writing within 30 days.
rules.escalation: Everything observed during site visits, demonstrations or meetings treated as Confidential Information without identification or reasonable understanding.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1 protects information the Disclosing Party may "disclose or make available", without limiting its form; no annotation on the page addresses oral disclosure.

rules.title: Use limited to the purpose
rules.guidance: We must be able to carry out the evaluation the Purpose describes, including our internal planning.
rules.preferred: Use solely for the Purpose on the Cover Page, which covers evaluating the business relationship it describes.
rules.acceptable: A residuals clause permitting use of information retained in unaided memory, excluding patents and specifically identified trade secrets.
rules.escalation: A Purpose narrowed so the described evaluation cannot be carried out (for example excluding internal planning or review by the warehouse sites), or each use made subject to the Disclosing Party's prior consent.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 2(a). Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): "The Purpose limits how Confidential Information may be used", with examples from broad evaluation of a business relationship to narrow reviews of vendor security documentation. A residuals clause appears only as a Language Library option, without commentary.

rules.title: Sharing with employees
rules.guidance: Our employees who need the information for the evaluation must be able to see it without case-by-case approval.
rules.preferred: Disclosure to employees with a reasonable need to know for the Purpose, bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than the MNDA, the Receiving Party remaining responsible for their compliance.
rules.acceptable: A requirement that employees be told the information is confidential before they receive it.
rules.escalation: Disclosure to employees only with the Disclosing Party's prior consent, only to named individuals, or only after each signs an individual undertaking.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 2(b): employees and other representatives with a reasonable need to know, bound by obligations no less protective, the Receiving Party remaining responsible. No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Sharing with advisers and other representatives
rules.guidance: Our advisers and contractors work on the evaluation and must be able to see the information on the same terms as employees. Our responsibility for them is responsibility for their compliance, not more.
rules.preferred: Disclosure to agents, advisors, contractors and other representatives with a reasonable need to know, bound by obligations no less protective than the MNDA, the Receiving Party remaining responsible for their compliance.
rules.acceptable: Affiliates under common control added as permitted recipients on the same terms, or disclosure to contractors subject to consent not unreasonably withheld.
rules.escalation: No disclosure to advisers, contractors or other representatives without the Disclosing Party's prior consent at its discretion, or liability for representatives beyond responsibility for their compliance (for example an indemnity, or strict liability for any disclosure by them).
rules.source: Standard Terms section 2(b). Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): section 2 "does not extend to sister entities or affiliates"; the page suggests an edit adding affiliates under common control.

rules.title: Compelled disclosure
rules.guidance: If we are compelled to disclose, we give notice where the law allows and cooperate at the other party's cost, but we cannot be made to fight the order or pay for it.
rules.preferred: Disclosure to the extent required by law, regulation, subpoena or court order, with reasonable advance notice (where legally permitted) and reasonable cooperation at the Disclosing Party's expense.
rules.acceptable: An added obligation to disclose only the part legally required.
rules.escalation: Cooperation at the Receiving Party's own expense, an obligation to resist or challenge the order, notice required even where the law prohibits it, or disclosure barred until the Disclosing Party consents.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 4 (reasonable advance notice to the extent legally permitted; reasonable cooperation at the Disclosing Party's expense). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Confidentiality of the agreement and discussions
rules.guidance: The discussions are confidential both ways. Neither side may publicise them.
rules.preferred: The existence and status of the discussions and the information on the Cover Page are Confidential Information of each party.
rules.acceptable: The existence of the MNDA (but not the subject of the discussions) excluded from Confidential Information.
rules.escalation: A right for either party to publicise the discussions or name the other party without consent.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1: "Each party's Confidential Information also includes the existence and status of the parties' discussions and information on the Cover Page." No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Reverse engineering
rules.guidance: We will test the robots in our warehouses. Silence is our standard; a prohibition limited to the materials provided is tolerable; anything reaching ordinary testing or products we buy elsewhere is not.
rules.preferred: The MNDA is silent on reverse engineering.
rules.acceptable: An express prohibition on reverse engineering, decompiling or disassembling samples, prototypes or software provided under the MNDA.
rules.escalation: A prohibition reaching products or materials obtained other than from the Disclosing Party (for example commercially available products), or a prohibition on analysis or testing needed for the Purpose.
rules.source: The Standard Terms say nothing on reverse engineering; use is limited to the Purpose (section 2(a)) and no licence is granted (section 7). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Independent development
rules.guidance: We develop our own systems. Independent development must stay outside the MNDA, and the MNDA must not restrict our own work.
rules.preferred: Information the Receiving Party can demonstrate it independently developed without using or referencing the Confidential Information is excluded.
rules.acceptable: The same exclusion, demonstrated by contemporaneous written records.
rules.escalation: The exclusion removed, a presumption that similar information we develop is derived from the Confidential Information, or any restriction on developing or acquiring competing products.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 3(d), with the Receiving Party bearing the burden ("information that it can demonstrate"). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Information from third parties
rules.guidance: Information we rightfully obtain from others free of restriction is outside the MNDA.
rules.preferred: Information the Receiving Party can demonstrate it rightfully obtained from a third party without confidentiality restrictions is excluded.
rules.acceptable: The exclusion limited to third parties not known to the Receiving Party to be bound by confidentiality.
rules.escalation: The exclusion removed, or information obtained from third parties treated as Confidential Information.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 3(c), with the same burden. No annotation on the page.

rules.title: No licence or transfer of rights
rules.guidance: The MNDA moves no rights in either direction. Our own information, ideas and analyses stay ours.
rules.preferred: The Disclosing Party retains all intellectual property and other rights in its Confidential Information, and disclosure grants no licence.
rules.acceptable: A licence to the Disclosing Party to use feedback we choose to give on its products, without payment.
rules.escalation: Any assignment or licence to the Disclosing Party of our own information, ideas, improvements or analyses beyond that feedback licence.
rules.hardLine: An assignment of the Receiving Party's intellectual property.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 7. The page annotates section 8 (Disclaimer): the NDA "is meant for preliminary discussions, not product use".

rules.title: Return or destruction
rules.guidance: We return or destroy what we received on request, at our choice, and confirm it if asked; the mechanics must be workable.
rules.preferred: On expiry, termination or the Disclosing Party's earlier request we cease use; promptly after written request we destroy or return all Confidential Information, at our choice; we confirm compliance in writing if requested.
rules.acceptable: Return or destruction within a stated period of at least 10 business days after the request, with written confirmation on request.
rules.escalation: Return or destruction within fewer than 10 business days, return required where destruction would do, confirmation by sworn statement or officer's certificate, or destruction of backups outside their normal rotation.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 6(a) to (c) (cease use; return or destroy promptly after written request; confirm in writing if requested). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Copies
rules.guidance: Working copies are part of any evaluation. Silence is our standard.
rules.preferred: The MNDA is silent on copies.
rules.acceptable: Copies limited to those reasonably necessary for the Purpose, carrying the same markings.
rules.escalation: An absolute prohibition on copying, or a requirement to log, number or report every copy.
rules.source: The Standard Terms say nothing on copies; a copy of Confidential Information is itself Confidential Information under sections 1, 2 and 6. No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Non-solicitation
rules.guidance: A confidentiality agreement should not carry restrictive covenants; a non-solicitation belongs in a separate agreement, if anywhere.
rules.preferred: No non-solicitation, no-hire, non-compete or exclusivity provision.
rules.acceptable: A mutual non-solicitation of employees met through the discussions, for no more than 12 months, excluding general advertising.
rules.escalation: A one-sided non-solicitation, any no-hire, a restriction longer than 12 months, or one covering employees not met through the discussions.
rules.hardLine: A non-compete or exclusivity obligation binding either party.
rules.source: The Standard Terms have no restrictive covenant and say "Neither party has an obligation under this MNDA to ... proceed with any proposed transaction" (section 11); the page does not mention non-solicitation.

rules.title: Survival of obligations
rules.guidance: We need to know when our obligations end. A fixed period of about the market norm is our standard, with trade secrets protected while they remain trade secrets.
rules.preferred: A Term of Confidentiality of 2 years from the Effective Date, trade secrets protected until they are no longer trade secrets.
rules.acceptable: A fixed Term of Confidentiality of up to 3 years from the Effective Date, with trade secrets protected while they remain trade secrets.
rules.escalation: A Term of Confidentiality longer than 3 years from the Effective Date, perpetual protection for all information, or a period running from each disclosure or the last disclosure with no outer limit.
rules.source: Cover Page Term of Confidentiality and Standard Terms section 5. Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): "Early termination of the NDA does not shorten the Term of Confidentiality"; 74% use a fixed period, most commonly 2 years, and 26% perpetual; trade secrets protected until they stop being trade secrets; the Cover Page offers the period from the Effective Date or from the date of last disclosure. Common Paper 2026 SaaS contract benchmark report: confidentiality period fixed in 79%, two years in 75% of fixed periods.

rules.title: Retention after return or destruction
rules.guidance: We cannot purge backups or records we must keep by law or policy. Retention under those headings, still confidential, is our standard.
rules.preferred: Retention under standard backup or record-retention policies or as required by law, with the MNDA continuing to apply to what is retained.
rules.acceptable: Retention limited to copies required by law and copies held in automatic backups.
rules.escalation: An absolute obligation to return or destroy every copy, including backups and copies kept by law or under a record-retention policy.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 6, last sentence (retention under standard backup or record-retention policies or as required by law, the MNDA continuing to apply). No annotation on the page.
